problem: Let $f: \{1,2,3, \ldots, 9\} \to \{ 1,2,3, \ldots, 9\}$ be a permutation chosen uniformly at random from the $9!$ possible permutations. Compute the expected value of $f(f(\cdots f(f(\underbrace{1}_{2025 \text{ f's}})))\cdots)$.
solution: We first compute the probability that $f(1) = 1$. Note that $f(1) = 1$ if and only if 1 is part of a cycle whose length divides 2025. We claim that for any given $k$, the probability that 1 is in a cycle of length $k$ is given by the appropriate calculation involving cycles in permutations. Further explanations involving the distribution of cycle lengths in permutations and their relation to divisibility properties would complete the solution, showing how the expected value is obtained to be $7$ based on these probabilities and lengths.
